title: My First Cars, Trains & Planes Coloring Book: interior, cover, KDP listing and Amazon Ads kit

general-counsel-agent.note: All ten checks on file. Pen name JONNY COLOR keeps the owner anonymous. Nothing commits the owner: no publishing, price or ad spend. The trademark note is a web screen, not a clearance; the owner decides before publishing. Topic note: the planned rotation has ended, so Trend Scout picked vehicles (cars, trains, planes and boats) under the owner's standing 'different topics' directive; no earlier book, record or DB books doc has it. Trucks were left out because the owner's own first book is Trucks, and none of the 30 subjects repeats a vehicle drawn elsewhere in the series (toy car, toy train, toy plane, toy boat, sailboat, submarine, rocket, hot air balloon, safari truck, camper, tractor, canoe, bicycle, scooter, sled). The working title 'Things That Go' was dropped because 'My First Things That Go Coloring Book' and 'My 1st Coloring Book: Things That Go!' already exist. The owner can swap the topic.

advertising-consumer-protection-counsel.note: Description, back cover, A+ points and ad texts checked against the built book: 30 subjects in four groups (9 road + 6 rails and cables + 7 air + 8 water) exactly as listed, 64 pages, blank backs, name labels and the 'Great job!' certificate are all true. 'Every page has ... a happy face' is true: all 30 pictures have faces. Every named example in the subtitle, description, back cover, ad texts and headlines (car, steam train, airplane, tugboat, school bus, helicopter, taxi, high-speed train, blimp, cruise ship) is in the book. The title says cars, trains and planes and the subtitle, tagline and description say boats are inside too, so nothing is hidden or overstated. No 'bestselling', review or result claims.

email-anti-spam-compliance-counsel.note: No commercial email. The delivery goes only to the owner.

privacy-data-protection-counsel.note: No personal data in the book, listing or ads kit; the 'This book belongs to' line collects nothing.

copyright-fair-use-counsel.note: Art is original vector drawing in art/vehicles.js; line and color contact sheets reviewed at full size. Generic vehicles only: no car maker's shape, grille, badge or name, no airline or rail livery, no cruise or ferry line markings, no police department or city crest (the police car has a plain star), and the taxi uses a plain checker band. The ambulance carries a heart instead of a red cross or star of life, both protected emblems. Fredoka font is SIL OFL 1.1, which allows embedding. AI-art note: purely AI-made pictures and text can't be registered for US copyright (US Copyright Office guidance; Thaler v. Perlmutter, D.C. Cir. 2025), so others may be able to copy the pages.

trademark-brand-clearance-counsel.note: Web search only (USPTO is unreachable from this environment). No book is titled 'My First Cars, Trains & Planes Coloring Book'; nearest are 'Cars, Trains, and Planes Coloring Book' (Jupiter Kids), Dover's 'Things That Go Coloring Book: Cars, Trucks, Planes, Trains and More!' and 'Colour the Cars, Trains, Trucks & Planes', all different titles, and the descriptive words can't be owned for a book's contents. 'MY FIRST CARS' (serial 90210585) was abandoned in 2021; no 'MY FIRST TRAINS' or 'MY FIRST PLANES' mark turned up. 'Cars' and 'Planes' are also Disney film titles: here they are plain plural nouns next to 'Trains', with no characters, eyes-on-windshield styling, fonts or colors from those films, so this is descriptive use; 'disney', 'pixar', 'lightning mcqueen', 'thomas the tank engine', 'paw patrol', 'hot wheels' and 'lego' are ad negatives only, so ads stay off franchise searches. Keywords, ad keywords and headlines use no brand, author or character names. An optional USPTO search before publishing would settle it.

platform-terms-policy-counsel.note: KDP: the AI question must be answered Yes for images and text (in the listing and the email). Title on the cover matches the metadata title; 7 keywords of 45 characters or fewer, no brands, no 'bestseller' or 'free' style terms, no other authors or titles. Categories are real children's paths; the owner should confirm 'Cars, Trains & Things That Go' in KDP's category picker, since KDP's list can differ from the store's. Amazon Ads book policy: 3 custom texts (134, 130 and 115 characters) and 3 headlines (41, 39, 35) with no price, sale, 'free' offer, best-seller or review claims ('screen-free' describes the activity); ad keywords are generic searches; 41 negatives.

kids-content-coppa-counsel.note: General-audience children's book for ages 2-5; nothing is collected from children. Friendly pictures only: no crashes, no one in danger, no flashing-light or siren claims, the police car and ambulance just smile, and the kayak, rowboat and speedboat show no one in the water. No small-parts or safety claims are made.

contracts-commercial-terms-counsel.note: No contract, license purchase or terms accepted. Nothing is uploaded to KDP or Amazon Ads.

fixes_made: Working title 'My First Things That Go Coloring Book' already exists (and Peter Pauper's 'My 1st Coloring Book: Things That Go!'), so the book is titled 'My First Cars, Trains & Planes Coloring Book'.
Ambulance drawn with a heart instead of a red cross or star of life (protected emblems).
Race car: a numeral that read as a stray mark was removed; the number circle was moved off the front wheel.
School bus: a stop-sign knob that read as a stray bump was removed. Police car: the star sat under a wheel; it was moved up beside the face and the band was narrowed.
Motorcycle: the seat floated above the tank; it now sits on the tank, and the headlight is on the fork. Ice cream van: the cone read as a lollipop; it was made bigger with waffle lines.
Speedboat was too small to color; it was enlarged with a bigger face. Rowboat: the face was moved down off the plank line.
A+ 'Look inside' title wrapped behind the picture cards; it was shortened to 'Look inside: 30 vehicles to color!' and the book was rebuilt.
Ad negatives add disney, pixar, lightning mcqueen, thomas the tank engine, paw patrol, hot wheels and lego so ads stay off franchise searches.
owner_notes: Answer KDP's AI question Yes for images and text.
Confirm the 'Cars, Trains & Things That Go' category in KDP's picker.
Optional USPTO search on the title before publishing; 'Cars' and 'Planes' are also Disney film titles, used here only as plain words.
Purely AI-made pages can't be registered for US copyright.
